approachQuestion.prompt:
Report conflicts after each registry edit

Input: an ordered list of edits to an initially empty registry. An edit is either SET(id,value), replacing the value for id or inserting it, or REMOVE(id), deleting id if present and doing nothing otherwise. After every edit, append true to the output exactly when all currently stored values are distinct; append false otherwise. Repeating SET with the existing value leaves the registry unchanged.

Example 1: edits = [SET(2,8),SET(5,8),SET(2,3),REMOVE(5),REMOVE(9)]. Output: [true,false,true,true,true]. Example 2: edits = [SET(1,4),SET(1,4),REMOVE(1)]. Output: [true,true,true]. Example 3: edits = []. Output: [].

Constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 200,000 edits; ids and values are signed 32-bit integers. Input is immutable. Prefer the least expected total running-time growth, then avoid unnecessary asymptotic auxiliary storage. Integer hashing has expected amortized constant-cost operations under non-adversarial hashing.

options.text: Keep id→value and value→active frequency maps, deleting zero-frequency entries. Keep a count of values whose frequency is at least two. Before a replacement remove the old contribution, then add the new one; change the count only when a frequency crosses between one and two. Emit whether that count is zero.
options.feedback: The maps track current bindings rather than edit history. Only crossing the uniqueness boundary changes the aggregate; removing the old contribution also handles repeated assignments correctly.

options.text: Maintain the same binding and frequency maps with zero entries deleted, but after every edit scan all active frequency entries to check whether any exceeds one.
options.feedback: The state is correct for all edits, but the repeated scan is removable by tracking how many frequencies cross the uniqueness boundary.

options.text: Keep a set of values from all SET edits. Emit false whenever a SET value is already in the set; emit true after REMOVE.
options.feedback: [SET(1,4),SET(1,4)] must emit true twice: overwriting the same id creates no second active binding. Historical membership cannot represent active multiplicity.

options.text: Keep active frequencies, increment the new value on SET, and decrement on REMOVE; never decrement the previous value on a replacement.
options.feedback: [SET(1,4),SET(1,4)] incorrectly raises frequency 4 to two. SET replaces one binding rather than adding a second binding.

feedback.reason: Maintain an aggregate by applying old-state removal and new-state insertion exactly once per update.
details: Use an id-to-value map and a value-to-frequency map, deleting zero frequencies. Keep the number of frequencies at least two. On SET, remove any old binding contribution before adding the new one; on REMOVE, remove a contribution only if id exists. Update the counter when a frequency crosses one↔two, and append whether it is zero after each edit.
Remove an existing ID's old contribution before adding its replacement. The conflict aggregate changes only when a frequency crosses one to two or two to one; larger counts remain conflicting.

“Keep id→value and value→active frequency maps, deleting zero-frequency entries. Keep a count of values whose frequency is at least two. Before a replacement remove the old contribution, then add the new one; change the count only when a frequency crosses between one and two. Emit whether that count is zero.”: The maps track current bindings rather than edit history. Only crossing the uniqueness boundary changes the aggregate; removing the old contribution also handles repeated assignments correctly.

“Maintain the same binding and frequency maps with zero entries deleted, but after every edit scan all active frequency entries to check whether any exceeds one.”: The state is correct for all edits, but the repeated scan is removable by tracking how many frequencies cross the uniqueness boundary.

“Keep a set of values from all SET edits. Emit false whenever a SET value is already in the set; emit true after REMOVE.”: [SET(1,4),SET(1,4)] must emit true twice: overwriting the same id creates no second active binding. Historical membership cannot represent active multiplicity.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method “Update frequencies and a conflict counter”, n is the number of edits and a is the maximum number of simultaneously active ids. Appending one boolean has amortized constant cost. Deleted entries release logical storage; map capacity is bounded by peak active entries. The output list contains n booleans. Choose its time and auxiliary-space pair. Use the tightest standard bound for the worst legal input of size n, with expected time over non-adversarial hashing. Fixed-width integer and fixed-size tuple hash operations take expected amortized O(1); arithmetic, comparison and copying one integer take O(1). Auxiliary space excludes the supplied input and returned result, includes all maps, sets, temporary copies and call stacks. The method is iterative, with constant call-stack space.
constraints: Use the tightest standard bound for the worst legal input of size n, with expected time over non-adversarial hashing. Fixed-width integer and fixed-size tuple hash operations take expected amortized O(1); arithmetic, comparison and copying one integer take O(1). Auxiliary space excludes the supplied input and returned result, includes all maps, sets, temporary copies and call stacks. The method is iterative, with constant call-stack space.

options.text: Expected O(n + 1) total time; O(a + 1) auxiliary space.
Expected O(n + 1) total time; O(n + 1) auxiliary space even when a is bounded.
Expected O(n² + 1) total time; O(a + 1) auxiliary space.
Expected O(n + 1) total time; O(1) auxiliary space.

feedback.reason: Apply constant expected map work per edit while retaining current bindings.
details: Maintain an aggregate by applying old-state removal and new-state insertion exactly once per update.
Each edit performs a constant number of expected amortized constant-cost map operations, threshold updates and output appends, giving expected O(n + 1) total time.

The binding map has at most a entries and the frequency map at most a positive-frequency entries. Under the stated deletion/capacity model this is O(a + 1) auxiliary space. The n returned booleans are excluded; no input copies or recursion are used.
“Expected O(n + 1) total time; O(a + 1) auxiliary space.”: Correct under the stated expected/amortized hashing model.

“Expected O(n + 1) total time; O(n + 1) auxiliary space even when a is bounded.”: The n booleans are returned output and excluded; deleted map entries are not retained. The tight auxiliary bound depends on peak active state.
“Expected O(n² + 1) total time; O(a + 1) auxiliary space.”: No full scan follows an edit; only a constant number of bindings and frequencies change.
“Expected O(n + 1) total time; O(1) auxiliary space.”: Arbitrarily many simultaneously active ids require retained bindings and frequencies.
